message.content:
**Winner:**  
Adele — *“25”*  

At the **59th Annual Grammy Awards**, held on Feb 12 2017, Adele’s studio album “25” took home the coveted **Album of the Year** trophy (the most prestigious “best‑album” honor offered by the Recording Academy).
message.reasoning:
The user asks "Who won the Grammy Award for Best Album in 2017?" They want the winner of the award category "Best Album" at the Grammys held presumably in early 2018 but awarding works from previous year; however they say 2017 which could refer to the ceremony or the album release year.

We need to interpret correctly. Usually the Grammys have categories like "Album of the Year". There isn't an official category called "Best Album", it's usually "Album of the Year".

But maybe they're referring to "Grammy Award for Best Album"? That might not exist as such. But we can answer with the winner of "Album of the Year" at the 59th Annual Grammy Awards (held February 12, 2017) honoring music released between September 1, 2015 and August 31, 2016. Winner was Adele – "25".

Alternatively, if they mean the 60th Annual Grammy Awards (February 10, 2018), awarded albums released between Sep 1 2016 - Aug 30 2017, winner was Beyoncé – "Lemonade".

Which one do they ask? They said "in 2017". So likely the awards given in 2017. That's the 59th Grammys. So answer: Adele's "25".

Let's provide context: It was the 59th Annual Grammy Awards, presented Feb 12, 2017, winner of Album of the Year was Adele for her album "25".

Also mention other winners perhaps. Provide details about the nomination list etc.

Thus produce concise answer.
